## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sedamocanagāthā* ("The sudorific verses") constitutes the twentieth chapter of the *Parivāra* in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. It comprises a series of Vinaya legal puzzles and riddles, traditionally considered so intricate and demanding that they cause the solver to sweat. In monastic jurisprudence, the text is cited in the commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) to settle difficult Vinaya determinations, such as legal edge cases regarding whether multiple instances of stealing across distinct shops collectively amount to a *pārājikā* offence [Bapat & Hirakawa 1970].

Automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus detects extensive overlap with the broader Vinaya literature, recording 269 matching passages across 18 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. It shares substantial textual segments with the Vinaya commentaries and treatises, foremost the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā* (31 matches), the *Pācittiya-aṭṭhakathā* (19 matches), the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* (16 matches), and the *Khuddasikkhā-mūlasikkhā* (16 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also draws upon or corresponds to rules in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, such as *Saṅghādisesa* 6 (30 matches) and *Pārājika* 4 (22 matches), as well as internal *Parivāra* sections such as the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further identifies cross-language matches with non-Pali canonical and paracanonical Vinaya texts, registering alignments with the Sanskrit *Poṣadhasthāpanavastu* (11 matches), Jayarakṣita's *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā*, and the Tibetan translation of the *Pratimokṣapadābhismaraṇa* (D4109) [DharmaNexus].
